result.summary: The contractor, Oscar Turner, has not replied to the job instruction sent on 1 Mar or to the three reminders sent on 4, 6 and 8 Mar, so the bedroom window job has stalled. I passed it to the ops team at normal priority. I recommended they phone him, find another contractor if he can't attend, and get the landlord's go-ahead first, because none is on record for the window. I also emailed the tenant to ask whether he has been in touch and whether the window can be secured, and set a hold to follow up in 2 days.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 026 flags no reply from the contractor after the job instruction (event 018) and 3 reminders (events 020-025). That is repeated non-response, so a person should step in, by phoning him or choosing another contractor. Separately, the landlord's only reply (event 010) is about a plumber at a different address and says nothing about the window. No approval is recorded, so ops should confirm the landlord's go-ahead before any quote goes ahead. The tenant can quickly tell us whether the contractor has contacted her and whether the window is secure, so I asked her.

alternatives_considered.option: Send a 4th reminder to the contractor
alternatives_considered.why_not: Three reminders by email and text have already gone unanswered. Another automated chase is unlikely to work.

alternatives_considered.option: Reassign to a new contractor myself
alternatives_considered.why_not: There is no other contractor on record for this property, and the landlord's go-ahead for the window isn't on record. A person should choose who to use and confirm with the landlord.
The classifier rates it routine (0.97), and nothing shows it is a ground-floor window or that the property is insecure. I asked the tenant to confirm.
